facts.fact: Search overview (secondary, ZBrush-origin methods): a common eye construction uses two spheres, one named Sclera and a duplicate named Cornea, with the cornea scaled slightly so it wraps the sclera.

Search overview: the iris area is masked and pushed inward to form a shallow concave dome on the sclera; the pupil is cleared and the edges are extended toward the eye centre; the cornea is masked over the same area and pushed outward into a smooth convex dome.
Search overview: iris fibres can be sculpted radiating from the pupil toward the outer iris edge with standard and damstandard brushes.
Blender Wikibooks guide (marked incomplete) suggests a sphere falloff shape for the iris sculpt, and an alternative of two balls where the iris bends inward from the inner ball.
Search overview: for the cornea shader, one source recommends a glass material with two-sided refraction enabled; without refraction the iris-to-cornea gap can look like empty space.
Search overview: a Blender-focused video covers modelling the cornea, iris, lacrimal caruncle and tear line; the caruncle and tear line were not documented in detail in retrieved snippets.

Emmetropic adult eye size (CT-based study, as summarised in search results): about 24.2 mm transverse (horizontal) x 23.7 mm sagittal (vertical) x 22.0-24.8 mm axial, with no significant difference between sexes or age groups.
Transverse eyeball diameter may range from 21 mm to 27 mm across adults; myopia or hyperopia mainly changes axial length.
Corneal horizontal diameter is about 11-12 mm and vertical diameter about 9-11 mm, so the cornea is wider than tall (horizontally oval).
A pooled estimate across studies gives a mean corneal diameter of 11.84 mm (SD 0.79 mm).
The limbus, the transition zone between cornea and sclera, is roughly 1-2 mm wide (search summary; primary figure not verified).
Corrected Scheimpflug photography study: anterior corneal radius 7.87 +/- 0.27 mm (SD) and posterior radius 6.40 +/- 0.28 mm (SD); posterior asphericity decreased significantly with age.

Scheimpflug photography in healthy adults aged 18-65 (search summary): anterior radius 7.79 +/- 0.27 mm and posterior radius 6.53 +/- 0.25 mm; both surfaces flatter horizontally than vertically. Exact source paper within the results was not confirmed.
Purkinje-image study in children aged 6-17 (search summary): vertical-meridian posterior radius 6.42 +/- 0.31 mm, range 5.62-7.22 mm. Source paper not confirmed.
Small study of 25 eyes aged 60-80 before cataract surgery (search summary): anterior radius R1 = 7.84 mm, posterior radius R2 = 6.4 mm.
Across the corneal curvature studies, anterior radius is about 7.8 mm and posterior about 6.4-6.5 mm; methods and sample sizes differ.

contradictions: Anterior corneal radius: 7.79 mm (Scheimpflug, 18-65) vs 7.87 mm (corrected Scheimpflug) vs 7.84 mm (small 60-80 cohort); differences are within method and sample variation.
Posterior corneal radius: 6.53 mm vs 6.40 mm vs 6.42 mm (children) vs 6.4 mm; not directly comparable across age groups and methods.
Some Blender-specific how-to details (two-sphere construction, glass with two-sided refraction) were in search overview text whose originating page was not confirmed for each claim.
